title: Equation of a Circle and Tangents
seo_title: Year 11 Maths: Equation of a Circle Worksheets (GCSE)
standard_text: Recognise and use the equation of a circle with centre at the origin; find the equation of a tangent to a circle at a given point.
meta_desc: Free Year 11 GCSE maths worksheets on the equation of a circle x² + y² = r²: the radius, points on a circle, gradients of radii and tangents, and equations of tangents. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: x² + y² = r² is a circle, centre (0, 0), radius r.
key_sub: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at that point.
body_html:
How it works

Every point (x, y) on a circle with centre the origin and radius r obeys x² + y² = r² (Pythagoras). So x² + y² = 49 has radius 7, not 49.

To find a tangent at P(a, b): the gradient of OP is b/a, the tangent is perpendicular, so its gradient is −a/b. Then use y − b = m(x − a).

Example

Find the radius of x² + y² = 81.

r² = 81

Answer: 9

Example

Find the gradient of the tangent to x² + y² = 25 at (3, 4).

Gradient of OP = 4/3

Perpendicular gradient = −1 ÷ 4/3

Answer: −3/4

Common mistakes

  • Giving r² as the radius.
  • Using the gradient of the radius for the tangent.
  • Forgetting the negative square root when a line crosses the circle.

faq.q: What is the equation of a circle with centre the origin?
faq.a: x² + y² = r², where r is the radius. It comes from Pythagoras' theorem.

faq.q: How do you find the equation of a tangent to a circle?
faq.a: Find the gradient of the radius to the point, take the negative reciprocal for the tangent, then use y − b = m(x − a).
